sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:52

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:52:1
items.html:
The Nukva is judgments, and she is of the aspect of the sorting of the kings — so how can the name “Nukva” rightly apply to Atik and AA, who are the utmost of mercy: You already know that all the Partzufim of Atzilut are considered as one Partzuf, as above in the words of the ARI (page 630, Item 35), that Atik and AA are considered only as the root for the Mochin of Atzilut, in which the coupling is made for the sake of those Mochin; and after they are formed there, they are born and come to their place, and they are called AVI of Atzilut. And those who receive the Mochin are called by the name ZON of Atzilut, who are the revelation of Atzilut, and from them the worlds are influenced. As above (page 630, the passage beginning “And All”).
And the reason for these matters you will understand according to their relation to the ten Sefirot of the direct light. For the upper phase of every Partzuf is the root of the Partzuf, and by its name the Partzuf is called; for example, if the upper phase is Keter, the whole Partzuf is called by the name Keter. And this indicates that the discernment of the Keter of the direct light rests upon the whole Partzuf, etc. — you will understand in this manner.
And therefore, in the Partzufim of Keter, it is impossible that the name Nukva will be there. For the name Nukva indicates a deficiency in her that requires completion by the male related to her. And this is possible only from Hochma and below, which is the discernment of a beginning of the expansion of the light from Ein Sof to the receiver. But Keter, which is the root and is the discernment of Ein Sof — meaning that the light has not yet been transferred to come into the category of a receiver, but stands in the discernment of a root, from which the light will expand to the receiver — so how can the name Nukva be fitting there?
And this is what he says: “So how can the name ‘Nukva’ rightly apply to Atik and AA, who are the utmost of mercy,” because they are the discernment of complete bestowal, where there is no discernment of reception at all. However, in truth there is no discernment of Nukva there at all, as he goes on to explain; rather, what we call by the name Nukva in this place also indicates, from the discernment of the root, that there is a bestowal unique to the male and a bestowal unique to the Nukva, and after these two roots we call them by the name of male and Nukva. As will be explained further on.
